newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Sasib shares suspended limit up.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Sasib shares suspended limit up.

text.p: Shares in Italian engineering firm Sasib Spa were suspended limit up on the Milan bourse on Monday after De Benedetti industrial holding company CIR announced it would make a public buy offer for Sasib shares.
Sasib shares had been suspended on the stock market by bourse watchdog Consob on Friday pending the announcement, having closed on Thursday at 4,900 lire per share.
They showed a theoretical value of 5,690 lire on Monday, some 16 percent up on the previous price, after the announcement on Saturday from financier Carlo De Benedetti's holding company.
Shares automatically trigger suspension if they hit 10 percent above or below the previous closing price.
CIR already holds 54.4 percent of Sasib's ordinary shares and its public buy offer (OPA) is for all ordinary and savings shares and convertible bonds held by minority shareholders.

It is offering 5,800 lire per ordinary share, 3,400 lire per savings share and 3,400 lire for each Sasib International BV bond expiring December 31, 1997 and convertible into Sasib savings shares at a rate of one for one.

CIR said the offer prices represented an increase of 26.8 percent on ordinary shares and 18.4 percent on savings shares compared with average prices for the stock registered on the bourse in the course of this month.
The OPA is expected to get underway at the start of June.
